question.text:
A student attempts to solve
$2\log_{2}x-\log_{2}x=3$.

Their working includes the statements
$2\log_{2}x=\log_{2}(2x)$ and $\log_{2}x=3\Rightarrow x=6$.

(a) Identify and explain the two errors.

(b) Solve the equation correctly.

display_blocks.content: (a) Identify and explain the two errors.

working.description: Identify the incorrect use of the power law.
Identify the incorrect conversion from logarithmic form.

a.answer: The power law is $2\log_b x=\log_b(x^2)$, not $\log_b(2x)$. Also, $\log_b x=3$ means $x=b^3$; multiplying 3 by the base is not the inverse logarithm operation.
